angle: This issue is about a commander who is a luxury and not a life-support system: a Goblin swarm that reads as chump blockers, an engine that turns one red mana into five cards — and three of five signed case files that resolve with Zada nowhere on the battlefield, so killing the hub costs you the draw engine and not the kill.

violators.text: SHE CAN DIE — YOU STILL WIN!

Tagline 'Goblins all the way down' from issue.json, verbatim. The dominant coverline names the most exciting verified thing in the book, the stack 005 loop; the kicker states the finding that organises the whole issue — that loop resolves with the commander off the battlefield. Both violators are true: 005 is a checker-passed unbounded loop, and three of the five case files never put her on the board. Vol. 001, August 2026, $4.95, decklist sha c8651652722c.

The Flight Plan: sections grouped under the five act headers, one lean row each — title, the promise verbatim from issue_spec, tier badge, byline. Print the tier legend and the three-columnist masthead in full; this is somebody's first issue by definition. No chart furniture — the map has to read in one glance.

departments.headline: GUARANTEED, NOT REQUIRED
departments.dek: Your commander is the one card you never have to draw. The Counselor reads the clauses that make that true — and then the record shows you a deck that spends the guarantee instead of leaning on it.
departments.body:
Start with the guarantee, because Commander gives you exactly one. CR 903.6 puts your commander face up in the command zone before a card is shuffled, and CR 903.8 lets you cast her from there — so Zada, Hedron Grinder is the only card in this issue you are never required to find. The schedule holds up: mean cast turn 4.352, median 4, exactly turn four in 7,002 of 10,000 goldfish runs, 90% by turn six. That is why your opening seven is allowed to be all fuel and no finisher.

Now read the bill. CR 903.8 charges an additional {2} for each previous cast from the command zone: four, then six, then eight. In a deck whose modal spell costs two and whose mean available mana on turn five is 4.589, a six-mana recast is three spells you did not cast — and spells cast is the only currency a storm count trades in. So the Counselor's finding and the Coach's instruction land on the same square. Buy protection on a quiet turn, where Swiftfoot Boots equips for {1}. Stop buying her back on a loud one.

Here is the part that makes this deck unusual at a Commander table: guaranteed access is not the same as required access. One of the three assembly targets the simulator tracks is gated on her, and of the five case files at the back of the book only A-001 and A-003 put her on the battlefield — A-002 kills through Impact Tremors, A-005 loops off Storm-Kiln Artist, and A-004 records her sitting in the zone for the whole turn. Colour identity keeps that honest: CR 903.4 reads only red off her cost and text, so the 99 holds no counterspell and exactly one answer to a resolved enchantment (Chaos Warp), and every slot the identity refuses buys another one-mana spell instead. As for CR 903.10a's 21-damage clock, a 3/3 needs seven clean connections — a coincidence, never a plan. Your clock is the wide board and the each-opponent effects. The table's clock is your turn-four window, and every opponent who can count Mountains has it circled. Let them watch the window. The deck does not live in it.

captions.Zada, Hedron Grinder: **EXHIBIT A:** a 3/3 for {3}{R} whose text never mentions winning — and the reason your opening hands are allowed to be all fuel, no payoff.
captions.Swiftfoot Boots: **THE INSURANCE POLICY:** hexproof and haste for {1} to equip, against {2} more every time you recast her. Buy it on the quiet turn or don't buy it.

pilot_tips.text: Equip Zada the turn before the engine turn, never the turn she lands — protection paid a turn early is protection you gave away.

departments.pull_quote: The command zone guarantees you one card. This deck is built so that card is a luxury.

departments.headline: CHUMP BLOCKERS, ALLEGEDLY
departments.dek: A table of veterans will look at your 1/1s and point its removal somewhere else. Take the gift — here's the game you're actually playing, in five moves.

callouts.title: SEED THE BOARD
callouts.text: Turns one through three, make Goblins and nothing else. Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command read as defense at a multiplayer table, and the simulator has an early token maker drawn in 60.0% of games at mean turn 3.18. Two 1/1s are not a threat — they are two extra copies of every spell you are about to aim at your commander.

callouts.title: LAND HER QUIET
callouts.text: Zada, Hedron Grinder arrives on turn four in 7,002 of 10,000 runs. Cast her as a four-mana 3/3, pass, and spend nothing. Firing a cantrip at her for two copies of value is how you buy a removal spell at full price.

callouts.title: ONE MANA, FIVE CARDS
callouts.text: The pivot is exact: Zada untapped, three or more other creatures, one red open. Case file A-001 signs the payload — one Crimson Wisps across four Goblins is five cards drawn and a hasted team for {R}. Fire it when the table's instant-speed answers are spent or tapped.

callouts.title: SHE DIES; YOU KEEP CASTING
callouts.text: Two of the three assembly targets never mention her, and A-002, A-004 and A-005 all resolve with her off the battlefield. When she eats removal, do not stop to rebuy her at {2} more and do not pass the turn sulking. Impact Tremors, General Kreat, the Boltbringer, Storm-Kiln Artist and Frontline Heroism are all still working.

callouts.title: PICK YOUR EXIT FIRST
callouts.text: Empty the Warrens under Impact Tremors takes 8 off every seat with no attack step (A-002). Fists of Flame turns the same board into 32 trample power (A-003). The Haze of Rage loop makes mana and pumps and by itself touches nobody (A-005) — fuel, not a kill.

captions.Zada, Hedron Grinder: **THE MULTIPLIER:** any instant or sorcery that targets only her is copied once for each other creature you control — a wide board turns one cantrip into mass draw.
captions.Dragon Fodder: **THE FUEL:** two 1/1s for two mana are two more copies off your next cantrip and two more damage triggers. The simplest card in the deck, and one of the most important.

pilot_tips.text: Hold Crimson Wisps until Zada has at least three coworkers — one {R} across four bodies is five cards, and the same spell on turn two is just a cantrip.

departments.pull_quote: Kill the hub and you have taken the draw engine. You have not taken the kill.

departments.headline: MOB RULES
departments.dek: Ten groups, ranked by job rather than alphabet: the case-file cards lead, the lands close, and every card gets one line on what it is actually for.

roster.role: The engine — Zada and her ammunition
The verified loop and the storm shelf
The payoffs that scale to three opponents
Lords, tutors, and the doubling cube

captions.Skullclamp: **ONE MANA, TWO CARDS:** every 1/1 token is a cantrip wearing a hat — the reason a sweeper is a draw step here instead of a loss.
captions.Brightstone Ritual: **EVERYONE PAYS:** {R} for each Goblin on the battlefield, and it counts theirs too. In the mirror, their swarm funds your storm turn.

pilot_tips.text: Feed Mogg War Marshal to a sacrifice outlet early — a token on entry and another on death makes him three bodies pretending to be one card.

departments.note: Grouped by job and ranked, verified engines first; the ten groups cover all 79 entries with no card unplaced. One thing to keep out of the reader-facing copy: synergy_graph.json gives Zada zero partners inside this 99, and 42 edges fall inside the deck overall. That is a fact about a global top-10 shortlist, not about the commander — no group ordering here is derived from it, and no caption may cite it.

departments.headline: BODIES AND MANA
departments.dek: Four hands, one call each. The keep rule takes 79.1% of first sevens, so the drill isn't courage — it's spotting the seven that's all crescendo and no verse.

hands.why: Three lands, bodies on two, a banked cantrip and an engine piece. This is the gold standard and it is not a dream hand: Goblins early, cheap spells always, and a commander who shows up at four mana whether you drew her or not.

Two lands and five spells that all want a game already in progress. Rituals need a board and storm needs a cast count, so this seven does nothing until some other hand builds the turn for it. It looks like the 26.5% ceiling and plays like a stalled car.

Two lands plus Sol Ring clears the keep rule, and Ruby Medallion is a storm multiplier disguised as a rock in a deck whose modal spell costs two. Bodies on two, a discount forever, and two payloads banked for the turn she lands.

A marginal seven rescued by its cheapest card: Faithless Looting trades the crescendo pieces for verse and stocks the graveyard on the way. Two tapped lands cost tempo this deck can afford — mean mulligans run 0.255, and this keep beats a blind six.

captions.Zada, Hedron Grinder: **THE ZONE SUBSIDY:** she is in none of these hands and all of them — four mana, always available, which is why your opener never needs a payoff.

pilot_tips.text: Count Faithless Looting as half a mulligan you did not have to take — it turns dead rituals into live bodies now and flashback fuel later.

departments.pull_quote: Your opener needs bodies and mana. It has never needed a win condition.

departments.headline: TWO TURNS, TWO TRAPS
departments.dek: Turn three with the engine still in hand; turn six with a wrath across the table. Commit to your line out loud before the Coach shows his — the reps are the whole exercise.

callouts.title: SPREAD ONE — TURN 3
callouts.text: Skirk Prospector out, three mana up, and a hand holding Dragon Fodder, Brightstone Ritual, Zada and Swiftfoot Boots. The control seat just tapped low; the token deck across the table looks far scarier than you do. Do you develop wide a turn early, or hold everything to land a protected commander?

callouts.title: SPREAD TWO — TURN 6
callouts.text: Zada online, four Goblins, Storm-Kiln Artist, {R}{R} open — and the Azorius player has exactly four mana up and three fresh cards. Crimson Wisps now, Wisps in response to the wrath, or no spells at all? The branches disagree about what a sweeper can actually take from you.

captions.Swiftfoot Boots: **THE HOLD QUESTION:** protection is real, and every turn it waits in hand the script it protects slips a turn. Spread one is about what insurance actually costs.
captions.Storm-Kiln Artist: **THE OTHER BANK:** whatever you decide about the wrath, magecraft Treasures survive it — both spreads lean on that fact from opposite directions.

pilot_tips.text: Count the copies before you cast: Zada copies for each OTHER creature you control, so four tokens is four copies plus the original — five draws, not four.

departments.pull_quote: A read you didn't make out loud is a read you didn't make.
departments.note: Two spreads from decisions/001 and 002. Hard rule: the recommendation renders only after every branch — neither headline, dek nor callout may telegraph it, which is why both callouts end on the question. Branch citations render with their verified treatment inside otherwise coaching spreads, exactly as the artifacts carry them.

departments.headline: FIVE CASES, ONE REFUSAL
departments.dek: Five questions went to the checker and five holdings came back. One is an unbounded loop, one is lethal to the exact point of state-based actions — and one takes the deck's most famous combo away.

callouts.title: CASE A-001 — THE BLUEPRINT
callouts.text: Crimson Wisps, Zada, four Goblin tokens, one red mana. The controlling clause is that her copies are put on the stack and never cast, so she cannot re-trigger on them and they raise no storm count. The holding: five cards drawn, five hasted creatures, {R} spent.

callouts.title: CASE A-002 — STORM MATH
callouts.text: Empty the Warrens as the fourth spell: storm sees three, three copies join the original, eight tokens enter, and Impact Tremors bills each opponent 8 — 32 down to 24, 28 down to 20, with no attack step anywhere. Cast Grapeshot afterward and it sees storm count 4, not 8: the copies were never cast. Count your casts.

callouts.title: CASE A-003 — EXACTLY LETHAL
callouts.text: Fists of Flame copies resolve one at a time, each drawing before it buffs, so the pumps lock in ascending — 3, 4, 5, 6 on the tokens and 7 on Zada, for 32 trample power off a board of 1/1s against a seat at 30. The checker withheld the stamp until the record walked the final step: state-based actions end the game, not the combat damage step. When your math is exactly lethal, walk that step every time.

callouts.title: CASE A-004 — THE REFUSAL
callouts.text: The databases promise that Krenko, Mob Boss plus Skirk Prospector plus Goblin Warchief is infinite. The loop needs to recast Krenko out of the graveyard through the command zone, and that rule serves commanders only — Zada holds the seat, so a sacrificed Krenko stays dead. What survives review: {1}{R}{R} under Warchief, haste, one activation, five tokens, ten Goblins on the board and up to ten one-shot red mana.

callouts.title: CASE A-005 — THE TRUE INFINITE
callouts.text: Haze of Rage with buyback plus Storm-Kiln Artist, and your commander is not on the battlefield for any of it. Cast one makes 3 copies and 4 Treasures; cast two makes 4 copies and 5 Treasures; buyback returns the card and only the card. Every iteration costs 4 Treasures and yields k+3, so it is mana-positive and strictly improves without bound.

captions.Haze of Rage: **THE PAYOFF:** two casts in, you hold the card, nine Treasures and a 20/2 paymaster — and every loop after this one is better than the last.
captions.Storm-Kiln Artist: **THE PAYMASTER:** a Treasure for every instant or sorcery you cast OR copy. Zada's copies count and storm's copies count — that clause is the whole economy.
captions.Fists of Flame: **THE ASCENDING BLADE:** each copy sizes its buff on its own resolution, so later copies draw deeper and hit harder. Nothing revises retroactively.
captions.Krenko, Mob Boss: **THE BURST, NOT THE LOOP:** one activation, and a Krenko fed to Prospector is gone for good in this deck. We checked.

pilot_tips.text: Never sacrifice Krenko to Skirk Prospector — he is not your commander, so he stays in the graveyard.

departments.pull_quote: Count your casts, not your resolutions.
departments.note: The issue's peak and the payoff to Act II — the most ambitious layout in the book, one feature spread per case in stack order. The refutation (A-004) is celebrated rather than buried, per house style, and A-005's headline fact is that the loop runs with the commander off the battlefield. Rules citations stay out of the body; every spread ends on its dossier pointer (FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-00N).

departments.headline: NOBODY FEARS A 1/1
departments.dek: Three opponents will agree that killing your commander kills your deck. That conclusion is the most useful thing you own — here's how to keep them holding it.

callouts.title: YOUR COVER STORY IS TRUE
callouts.text: You average 2.36 bodies on turn three. A Prospector and two tokens is a board nobody wraths and nobody fears, and it is also, precisely, the fuel tank. Deploy it face up and let the read stand.

callouts.title: LET THEM PAY FOR THE WRONG CARD
callouts.text: Everyone at the table has one plan for you: kill the four-mana Goblin. Let them buy it — a premium removal spell aimed at Zada is a card they will want back later. Cast her, pass, and let them spend.

callouts.title: THE TELL LADDER
callouts.text: What a table answers on sight, in order: Skullclamp, because it screams engine; Conspicuous Snoop, because he shows your library top for the rest of the game; Krenko, because everyone has heard the word infinite. Sequence the loud pieces after removal has found other homes — and play Impact Tremors early, onto one Goblin, where it pings for one and reads as durdle.

callouts.title: THE KRENKO DISCOUNT
callouts.text: The databases promise a Krenko loop this deck cannot run; A-004 records it terminating after one activation. So when an opponent burns real removal on him expecting the infinite, they have paid a card for a one-shot. Take the trade and say nothing.

captions.Conspicuous Snoop: **THE INFORMATION TAX:** he casts Goblins off your library top and shows the whole table what is coming, all game. Price that in before he hits the felt.
captions.Grenzo, Havoc Raiser: **THE OUTSOURCED DEFENSE:** every connecting Goblin goads a would-be blocker or exiles a card off that player's library for you. The cheapest way to point three armies anywhere but here.

pilot_tips.text: Deploy Skullclamp on the turn you intend to use it, not the turn you draw it — it is the loudest tell in the 99 and it draws removal the way it draws cards.

departments.pull_quote: The gap between what your board says and what your hand is building is your entire early game. Protect the gap, not the commander.

departments.headline: WHO ACTUALLY BEATS THE SWARM
departments.dek: Combo owns the clock, wraths walk into your draw engine, and the aggro seat was never your problem. Know which chair is dangerous before you sit down.

threats.read: The seat that beats you. Your own ceiling is a 26.5% line at mean turn 4.91 — live, but not a clock you can promise anybody — so do not plan to out-race a deck that assembles on purpose. Your interaction is 13 copies covering two of the five permanent classes, which means you disrupt once, cheaply, at the decisive moment. Rank the seats by combo proximity rather than board presence, apply pressure so their tapped-out setup turn costs them, and point Grenzo's goad at whoever is closest to going off. Held answers rot; the last profitable moment is now.

Taxes attack your arithmetic rather than your creatures: a two-spell turn that becomes a one-spell turn has halved the engine, so recount your hand under the tax before you commit to anything. You are the beatdown here, racing the lock's assembly. Name the out before you need it — Vandalblast overloads for {4}{R}, Goblin Trashmaster sacrifices a Goblin to kill an artifact, Chaos Warp answers the class nothing else here touches — and aim at the piece beating you, not the piece scaring you. Mana denial hurts less than the table assumes: Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual scale off bodies, not lands.

Your engine is wrath insurance rather than a wrath victim. Cards in hand and Treasures on the battlefield sit in two zones a creature sweeper cannot reach, so when the wrath is telegraphed at sorcery speed, fire the cantrip engine and bank the draws — A-001 is the whole argument, and decision spread two walks this exact board. Holding back is the loss, because time is their plan. Then charge rent for the sweeper itself: Skullclamp turns each dying 1/1 into two cards, Pashalik Mons pings per Goblin death, Goblin Bombardment converts the rest on the way out. Keep one token maker in hand at all times.

Take the control seat and stop trying to be bigger. Mean bodies of 4.07 by turn five and 5.26 by turn six give you a blocking wall while the engine sets up, and 40 life absorbs the early turns. Blasphemous Act costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield, which in this pod is a two-mana reset and you are the only seat built to rebuild from one. Gempalm Incinerator cycles for damage equal to every Goblin on the battlefield, theirs included, so read the whole board before you name a target. Then win where blockers are irrelevant, through Impact Tremors and General Kreat.

pilot_tips.text: In the token mirror, read Brightstone Ritual again — it counts every Goblin on the battlefield, so the opposing swarm pays for your storm turn.

departments.pull_quote: Against combo the last profitable moment for an answer is now. Against everyone else it is later than you think.

departments.headline: TWO WISHES, ONE TRIBE
departments.dek: Both your tutors wish in one colour and one creature type, and that is a strength — every wish is on plan. Just don't send the wrong Goblin on the errand.

captions.Goblin Matron: **THE ERRAND RUNNER:** any Goblin CARD to hand, which includes Gempalm Incinerator's removal and Boggart Shenanigans. Delivery to hand means the fetch still gets cast — kicker still gets paid, cycling still works.
captions.Moggcatcher: **THE REPEATABLE WISH:** a Goblin permanent straight onto the battlefield for {3} and a tap — no cast, nothing to counter, and no kicker either. Time him like a land, a full rotation before you want the wish.

pilot_tips.text: Fetch Goblin Bushwhacker with Matron, never Moggcatcher — kicker is paid as you cast, and a Bushwhacker put onto the battlefield is a 1/1 with stage fright.

departments.pull_quote: Finishers to hand with Matron; engines to the battlefield with Moggcatcher.
departments.note: Data renders from tutor_guide.json — scenario / fetch / why entries across the two tutors. Two threads worth keeping visible in the layout: neither wish needs the commander, which is the issue's thesis showing up in the search engine; and no wish reaches the storm half at all, because that component is built out of sorceries and no Goblin tutor has ever named one. Aim the wish at the early-token component, which assembles in 60.0% of runs at mean turn 3.18 and three of whose five cards are Goblins.

departments.headline: THIRTY-THREE RED SOURCES, ONE LOUD TURN
departments.dek: Thirty-three of the 36 lands make red, eight enter tapped (22%, inside the usual budget), and lands alone put red on curve 86.9% of the time. So the audit's question was never whether the mana arrives — it's what 43 sources and six rituals buy on the one turn you choose.

captions.Skirk Prospector: **THE CONVERSION DESK:** a Goblin becomes {R} on demand with nothing on the stack to answer — and he is counted among the 43 sources, unlike the rituals beside him.
captions.Battle Hymn: **NOT A SOURCE, A SPIKE:** {R} for each creature you control, once. Rituals do not add mana per turn, they add mana to one turn — which is the only unit a storm count trades in.

pilot_tips.text: Cast spells with Throne of Eldraine's four red and pay Skullclamp's equip or Goblin Burrows' pump with mana from somewhere else.

departments.pull_quote: You are not building a mana base. You are building a fuse.
departments.note: Data renders from mana_analysis.json plus the writer's mana_base prose: 69 red pips across 57 cards, effective pip requirement 2, 33 red land sources against a 36-source yardstick, 43 sources once rocks and dorks are counted, on-curve 86.9% from lands alone and 96.0% with rocks and dorks, 8 of 36 lands entering tapped (5 of them unconditionally). Ledger's framing holds: the target is a yardstick, not a grade — a mono-red deck whose heaviest ask is {R}{R} does not need the thirty-sixth source the way a triple-pip deck would. The stated-assumptions box says exactly what the hypergeometric model does and does not audit. The declared art break renders after this section.

departments.headline: TEN THOUSAND GOBLINS
departments.dek: We ran the list 10,000 times on seed 42. The window is turn four in seven games of ten, the floor is a draw engine that shows up two games in three, and the ceiling is one game in four — plan for the floor.

callouts.title: THE WINDOW
callouts.text: Commander mean cast turn 4.352, median 4 — exactly turn four in 7,002 of 10,000 runs, 90% by turn six. That is a schedule rather than a hope, and every opponent who can count Mountains has the same schedule.

callouts.title: THE FLOOR
callouts.text: An early token maker is drawn in 60.0% of runs at mean turn 3.18, bodies average 5.26 by turn six, and 'Zada online with a cantrip' assembles in 66.1% — 49.6% by turn six, mean turn 5.27. Wide pressure plus mass draw is the median game, and the median game is the one you pace for.

callouts.title: THE CEILING IS ONE GAME IN FOUR
callouts.text: 'Storm payoff plus ritual drawn' assembles in 26.5% of runs, 16.9% by turn six, mean turn 4.91. It reads lower than the other two for a structural reason: it is the only target that is an AND of two independent four-card groups, so both halves have to arrive. Treat the storm kill as opportunism you take when it comes to you.

callouts.title: THE LANDS QUIT EARLY
callouts.text: Land drops fall to 63.7% by turn five and 54.2% by turn six, and mean available mana still climbs — 3.937 on turn four, 4.589 on five, 5.182 on six. After the opening turns this deck's mana growth is rituals, Treasures and Goblins rather than land drops, which is exactly why the audit next door calls the base a fuse.

captions.Idol of Oblivion: **THE UNMODELED ENGINE:** a card for every turn you made a token. The simulator draws one card a turn and still likes this deck; your real games draw more.
captions.Haze of Rage: **IN THE GROUP NOW:** the storm-payoff component counts four cards, this one among them — which is why the ceiling reads 26.5% instead of something thinner.

pilot_tips.text: Get Reliquary Tower down before the engine turn — the simulator never fills a hand past seven, and case file A-001 will.

departments.pull_quote: The storm kill is the ceiling. The draw engine is the floor, and the floor wins the median game.
departments.note: The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and prints all model assumptions verbatim: this is resource development, not games. Keep rate 79.1%, mean mulligans 0.255, seed 42, 10,000 iterations — quote every figure exactly as the artifact reports it. The simulator models no rituals, no cost reducers and no extra draw, so 26.5% is the conservative reading of the ceiling and the box has to say so.

departments.headline: FAME ISN'T DOING THE SORTING
departments.dek: Ten cards worth knowing about, ranked by how much of each line is already in the 99. Their EDHREC ranks span 76 to 13,958, which tells you how little that number decided.

callouts.title: THE METHOD
callouts.text: Each entry is scored on adjacency to something the checker already signed — the copy-draw engine (A-001), the storm burst (A-002), the Haze loop (A-005). A card that finishes a line whose other pieces are already in the deck outranks a famous card that arrives alone. Three of the ten answer a measured weakness instead: Soul-Guide Lantern is the only pick that moves the interaction-breadth count, from two answered permanent classes to three, and Deflecting Swat plus Champion's Helm are the protection budget.

callouts.title: THE HEADLINE SCOUT
callouts.text: Reiterate is the cleanest arithmetic on the page: one card sits at the end of three separately flagged infinite lines, and every other piece those lines name — Mana Geyser, Seething Song, Ruby Medallion, Storm-Kiln Artist — is already in the 99. Off-combo it buyback-copies Mana Geyser on the pivot turn, which is the biggest single mana swing this deck can make.

callouts.title: SEVEN CLAIMS, ZERO SIGNATURES
callouts.text: Reiterate's three lines, Thornbite Staff's three and Seething Anger's one are flagged infinites and nothing more. The status field on every one of them reads 'needs a stack scenario', and it means that literally — none has been through the checker, so none is stated as fact anywhere in this issue.

callouts.title: THE HONEST REFUSALS
callouts.text: Lightning Greaves grants shroud, which stops your own Crimson Wisps from targeting Zada — it is the wrong equipment for a deck whose plan is targeting its own commander, and Champion's Helm's hexproof is why it made the page instead. Repercussion turns your own Blasphemous Act into 13 damage per 1/1, aimed at your face. Reputation does not survive contact with rules text.

pilot_tips.text: Hold Blasphemous Act as your reset, never as spot removal — every creature on the battlefield knocks {1} off its {8}{R}, so eight bodies across the pod make it a one-mana wrath, and you are the only seat built to rebuild from one.

departments.pull_quote: A card that finishes a line already in your 99 beats a famous card that arrives alone.
departments.note: Data renders from considering.json — ten entries, and no ownership chip anywhere on the page: whether the reader owns a card is not this magazine's business, and the section says nothing about anybody's collection. Every entry carries a bracket delta of 4 to 4; Jeska's Will is the only Game Changer among them and does not shift the computed floor either. Worth surfacing in the layout: the obsolescence channel came back empty for this deck — its tightest match, 0.9877, is Dragon's Desire against Mana Geyser, which quietly changes the bet rather than upgrading it.

departments.headline: READ THE FILES YOURSELF
departments.dek: The complete record: every step, every citation verbatim, checked against the June 19, 2026 rules. The Counselor read them twice so you can cite them once.
departments.note: Renderer-generated from the checker-passed artifacts; nothing summarised, truncated or paraphrased, every citation verbatim in typewriter face. A-001 (Crimson Wisps engine; pass, 1 review cycle): copies put on the stack, five draws, team haste. A-002 (Empty the Warrens storm turn; pass, 1 cycle): storm sees three, eight tokens, 8 to each opponent through Impact Tremors, and a following Grapeshot sees storm count 4. A-003 (Fists of Flame lethal; pass, 2 cycles): ascending per-resolution buffs, 32 trample power, and the state-based-action step the checker demanded before stamping — print the cycle count as case status, because it is the system working. A-004 (Krenko burst; pass, 1 cycle): the database's infinite refuted for this deck, with the surviving burst quantified. A-005 (Haze of Rage loop; pass, 1 cycle): the unbounded loop, k+3 Treasures per iteration against a four-Treasure cast, with the commander in the command zone throughout.

departments.headline: THE WIZARD OF BARGE
departments.dek: Fifty-six hands painted this deck and one of them painted fourteen cards, your commander included. The count is per card, the provenance is printed, and the copies get their own line.

featured.note: The ledger first. Wizard of Barge painted 14 of this deck's 79 entries — 17.7%, with the runner-up at four — and those 14 entries account for 35 of 100 copies, which is a separate fact on its own line because 22 of those copies are one Mountain painting counted once. Now the provenance, printed plainly: 13 of the 14 sit in a single contiguous Secret Lair collector-number run, 2406 through 2418. That is a product bought whole, not a gallery assembled card by card, and saying so is better than inventing taste. It is also the better story, because of what happened to be inside the box: Zada herself, Krenko, Skirk Prospector, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot, Skullclamp, Conspicuous Snoop, Roaming Throne, Sol Ring — the commander, the burst, the refuted loop and the storm payoffs this issue verifies, all in one irreverent hand. Everything else disperses completely: 56 artists across 79 entries, 62 of those entries printed through The List by 52 different painters. One purchase gave this deck a house style. The credits page just declines to call it curation.
featured.hero_caption: **THE COMMANDER'S PORTRAIT:** Wizard of Barge's Zada — the card this whole issue argues is a draw engine in a trench coat, painted like she is in on the joke.

also_worth_noting.note: Four entries and the honest runner-up: Goblin Matron, Mogg War Marshal, Quest for the Goblin Lord and Reliquary Tower — the tutor, the fodder, the anthem and the land that holds the drawn cards.
Three entries across three jobs: Goblin Negotiation's removal, Grenzo, Havoc Raiser's politics and Swiftfoot Boots' insurance.

captions.Krenko, Mob Boss: **SAME HAND, SAME MOB:** the burst that A-004 quantifies, from the same brush as the commander — one drop, one house style.
captions.Skullclamp: **THE EQUIPMENT PORTRAIT:** the loudest tell in the 99, painted by the artist who did the whole engine room.

departments.pull_quote: One drop bought whole, thirteen cards in a row. We print the collector numbers, not a myth about taste.
departments.note: The renderer recomputes every count from artist-credits; the figures here must match it exactly. Art File fast-facts: 79 entries, 100 copies, 56 artists; top sources The List (62 entries, 52 artists) and Secret Lair Drop (17 entries, 4 artists); treatments 14 borderless, 14 foil, 14 inverted frames, 7 legendary, 1 spree. Count per card, never per copy, and respect the command's notes[] verbatim — the concentration is structural, and the drop_runs entry is the evidence for saying so.

NEXT ISSUE: HAPATRA, VIZIER OF POISONS, from issue.json verbatim — tease the pivot from one-mana mass draw to one-drop snakes without inventing content. Colophon: rules version June 19, 2026; decklist sha256 c8651652722c…; goldfish seed 42, 10,000 iterations; generation provenance; Fan Content Policy line. Close on the ledger rather than a flourish: the whole claim record in this issue is five case files and one simulator, and both are printed in the back of the book.

rhythm_notes: The five acts carry the tempo and I did not fight them. Act I meets the deck and steps down in density — instruction (Command Zone), narrative (Game Plan), browsing (The 99) — so the reader has flipped through the 99 before anybody asks them to mulligan. Act II runs practice into participation and lands on The Kill, which is the peak of the book and the payoff to both: here is how you fly it, here is what it kills with, and its own internal rhythm alternates narrative case files against the dossier boxes. Act III is three consecutive Coach sections and reads as one long conversation at the table; Act IV is three consecutive Ledger ones and is where the only dense-dense adjacency lives — Sources Say into By the Numbers — which the renderer's declared full-bleed art break covers. That break wants commander art at full bleed and a single computed Ledger line, nothing more. Act V cools deliberately: the reference wall of Judge's Desk, then appreciation in Featured Artist, then a quiet Back Page. Two furniture caps I held to on purpose: no section carries more than five callouts, and the four puns in the book (chump blockers, the errand runner, the conversion desk, the information tax) all live in furniture, never in a rules explanation or a data caption.
gaps: Roaming Throne naming Goblin against Zada's copy trigger needs a stack scenario — genuinely unsettled (does the extra trigger produce a second full copy set, and what does each copy then target?), and it is the highest-value checker fodder in the deck. Both cards are in the 99 and no combo line contains the pair.

Frontline Heroism and Zada triggering off the same cantrip needs a stack scenario: you order your own triggers, so whether Zada counts the Soldier that Heroism just made is worth one card per cast on a lethal turn. Until it resolves, the second copy hub is described by oracle text only.

Past in Flames as a second-wave storm turn needs a stack scenario before any 'second payoff' claim can leave coaching tier — the open questions are the exact storm count the second payoff sees and whether the mana nets positive.

Ancestors' Aid on Zada as a ritual rather than a pump spell needs a stack scenario — one Treasure per copy, plus a magecraft Treasure per copy with Storm-Kiln Artist, is potentially mana-positive on a four-body board.

The Short List carries seven flagged infinites across three cards (Reiterate ×3, Thornbite Staff ×3, Seething Anger ×1) and zero verifications. Any one of them resolved would change what that section is allowed to say; today none of them may be stated as fact.

synergy_graph.json gives Zada zero partners inside this deck and 42 edges fall inside the 99 overall. It is a global top-10 shortlist rather than a per-deck fit score, so nothing in this issue is grounded on it — worth stating to the next editor so the channel is not mistaken for silence about the commander.

card_roles.json has no pattern for ten cards in this deck — Chaos Warp, Crimson Wisps, Daring Discovery, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Past in Flames, Reliquary Tower, Renegade Tactics, Spreading Insurrection and Wild Ride. Absence of a role is not absence of the function: several of those draw cards, which is why the taxonomy's card-advantage count reads lower than the deck actually plays.

How many protection slots to buy is unsettled between two strategy sections (5-7 against 2-4), and the answer depends on what removal these tables actually run. A deck_recon pass would settle it; until then the issue prices protection as a purchase for the Zada draw turns specifically rather than as a standing tax.

Strategy DB holes the frame names, all four worth a research pass: goad and forced combat as compulsion rather than persuasion (Grenzo); aristocrats-style sacrifice conversion and what free outlets do to overextension math; hub redundancy for a copy engine specifically (Frontline Heroism standing in for a legendary hub); and storm critical-mass theory under a tax.
